result:
The proposed answer of 1/8 is not correct. The limit should be 1/10.

**Structure of the graph.** Identify the vertex {i, j} with i < j with the grid point (i, j). Adjacency is a unit step in either coordinate, so T₂(Pₙ) is an induced triangular (staircase) region of the square grid. It has about n²/2 vertices.

**Domination density.** The infinite square grid has domination density 1/5, achieved by the perfect-domination pattern. In a region of area A, the domination number is therefore about A/5, plus a boundary correction of order O(perimeter). The region here has perimeter O(n), so the correction is O(n). This gives

γ(T₂(Pₙ)) = (1/5)(n²/2) + O(n) = n²/10 + O(n).

So the limit is 1/10.

**Flaws in the proposed solution.** The claim that γ ≈ n²/8 "based on several studies" has no support. The listed small values (1, 2, 3, 5) are too small to separate n²/8 from n²/10, since O(n) boundary terms dominate at those sizes. Nothing in the argument shows the density 1/5 fails in the interior of the region, and it cannot fail there.

VERDICT: REJECT
